title: Concrete coefficient series, restricted matrices and finite tests
statement:
Use the exponent vectors, generated diagrams, first-vertex supports, degree prefixes and essential variables of [def-trf-supported-homogeneous-division]. For a commutative ring $A$, a field $L$, $m,n,s\in\mathbf N$, coefficients $c_{i\gamma}\in A$ and a ring map $T:A\to L[[W_1,\ldots,W_m]]$, put
$$[W^\delta Z^\gamma]f_i=[W^\delta]T(c_{i\gamma}).$$
Here series mean [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] and polynomials mean [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. For any finite variable set $S$ put $E_t(S)=\{e\in\mathbf N^S:|e|=t\}$. Assign the division index $(i,\beta)$ the exponent $\alpha_i+\beta$, and a remainder index its exponent. For any linearly ordered vertex index set, define a square matrix on $E_t(S)$ by taking, at column $e$, the coefficient vector of a supported-family index assigned to $e$ when one exists, and zero otherwise. Use classical choice to select such an index; for ordered vertex families it is unique. In the prefix $I_q=\{i:|\alpha_i|\le q\}$ with essential variables $S_q$, define
$$h_{i,q}=\sum_{e\in E_{|\alpha_i|}(S_q)}c_{i,\iota_*e}Z^e\quad(i\in I_q),$$
where $\iota_*e$ extends $e$ by zero to the original $Z$ variables. Denote its square division matrix by $M_{q,t}$. For $B:\mathbf N\to\mathbf N$, let
$$F_B=\{c_{i,\alpha_i}:i\in\operatorname{Fin}(s)\}\cup\{\det M_{q,t}:0\le q\le d_{\max},\ 0\le t\le B(q)\},\qquad d_{\max}=\max(\{0\}\cup\{|\alpha_i|\}_i).$$
Determinants mean [def-weil-endomorphism-determinant]. For global coefficients on a scheme $N$, define
$$S(\alpha,c)=\{b\in N:\ (c_{i\gamma})_b\in\mathfrak m_b^{|\alpha_i|-|\gamma|}\text{ whenever }|\gamma|<|\alpha_i|\},$$
where $(c_{i\gamma})_b$ is the germ and $\mathfrak m_b$ the maximal ideal of the local ring [def-weil-residue-field]. These are the eight existing concrete constructions extracted unchanged from the uniform-division module; no mathematical meaning changes.

source.place: Bierstone--Milman, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), Lemma 7.7 pp.263--264, Theorem 8.1 pp.273--275, and completion of Theorem 9.6 p.282. BM read online at https://mahalex.net/teaching/seminars/gabber/Bierstone-Milman%20Canonical%20desingularization%20in%20characteristic%20zero.pdf; ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 is the route reference.
